name: Facet
text: Adopt a dark theme by default, auto-switching to light only if the user manually toggles it. This maximizes visibility and liveliness in low-light conditions while reducing eye strain during long sessions. The trade-off is that some users may prefer light mode for readability in bright environments, but the manual toggle with a persistent reminder ("Light mode active—switch back") keeps control in their hands without cluttering the interface.

name: Pane
text: The real risk isn’t preference—it’s habituation. Users who override once won’t remember to switch back, leaving the interface in a state that fights their context. Instead, default to system preference and let users opt into dark mode. Settle it with a week-long A/B test measuring session length and error rates.
